findings.title: Command injection vulnerability
findings.description: The command-injection pattern is in a helper that opens a workflow URL. That URL comes from an internal service response, not direct user text; the process launch still has a shell-enabled branch. Validate the scheme and use an explicit argument list.

findings.title: Command-injection pattern from Python subprocess calls invoking bash -c
findings.description: There are three affected files; two alerts come from separate call sites in one file. The findings are in a deployment helper that logs in to a container registry and pushes a package, and two helpers build a cluster-configuration command. The values are Lambda environment variables set by infrastructure, not request parameters. Exploitability is low in this context; no user-input taint path was found.

findings.title: DiagSpill SCTP kernel exposure (CVE-2026-74469)
findings.description: Potentially vulnerable kernel 7.0.12-linuxkit with SCTP diagnostics reachable (sctp: loaded; sctp_diag: built-in). Local exploitation needs no capability or unprivileged user namespace; verify vendor backports. Mitigation: update the kernel, or hard-disable both sctp and sctp_diag if SCTP is unused.
findings.evidence: The observed LinuxKit kernel may be the Docker host kernel, not the Rocky image kernel.

findings.title: Missing Antiforgery C# API Exposed
findings.description: The vulnerability is a missing anti-forgery token on a state-changing HTTP POST MVC action, which exposes the endpoint to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks. Without the token validation, malicious sites could trick authenticated users into submitting unwanted requests.
